item: Recursive Hilbert-ball colouring p(T) of dyadic partitions (I19) and its pullback X_I^(n)(g) to F (I23), driven by a fixed-point-free Lipschitz map
lean_status_why: partitionColor (RecursiveColoring.lean:23) is the paper's p(T) with the same recursion, the same well-founded measure (cell count) and the paper's displayed choice of intervals (selectedInterval: depth 2D, odd indices), and every step the item drives (pullback globalColor, recursive identity, exact covariance, the generic correlation core, the explicit L^2([0,1];R^2) displacement map) lies on the proof DAG of the comparator theorem, whose statement matches the headline exactly; this was checked at text level only, without compiling.
lean_gaps: NOT COMPILED: there is no local toolchain and the comparator config has enable_nanoda=false. All checks here are text-level. A grep of the 68 Thompson files finds no sorry, admit or axiom.

Comparator vs internal results: the comparator asks only for a composition-compatible group structure on F with no InvariantMean. Main.lean also proves thompson_F_boundary_with_exact_constant and thompson_F_uniform_boundary, but they are not comparator targets. The item is on the comparator's chain either way.

Constants are NOT numerically explicit in the Lean. displacementLipschitzConstant depends on separationAtScale := Classical.choose (gamma_uniform_separation (1/32) _) (AnalyticConstruction.lean). The transports pairTransport are Classical.choose of exists_affine_pair_transport (TransportFamily.lean:41-59). So the Lean certifies an existential boundary constant boundaryConstant L (1/2) D, not a numeral. This matters for the explicit Folner and Kesten targets (S4, S5).

Route addition, not a gap: the forward Folner criterion (invariant mean => Folner sets) is proved in Lean (MeanApproximation, ProbabilityDefects, FiniteCoarea, MeanToFolner, about 10% of the DAG), where the paper cites it.

The selected intervals are fixed to selectedInterval D (depth 2D, index 2i+1). This is the paper's displayed choice (finite-proof.tex:121-123, I_j=[(2j-1)2^{-r},2j 2^{-r}]). partitionColor itself is generic in I : Fin D -> BasicInterval.

Carrier: F is a subtype of interval homeomorphisms with a dyadic PL witness (Model.lean:52). StandardCharacterization.standardPLEquiv identifies it with the standard finite-breakpoint model, so the formalisation is faithful.

lean_source.text: abbrev UnitBall (E : Type uE) [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] := {x : E // ‖x‖ ≤ 1}
lean_source.note: Carrier of the coloring: closed unit ball as a subtype.

lean_source.name: ballMean
lean_source.note: Equal-weight mean bundled with its unit-ball proof; the argument of f in the recursion.

lean_source.name: partitionColor
lean_source.kind: def (THE item: recursive Hilbert-ball coloring p(T))
lean_source.text:
def partitionColor (I : Fin D → BasicInterval) (hI : ∀ i, (I i).Internal)
    (hD : 0 < D) (f : UnitBall E → UnitBall E) (T : BasicPartition) :
    UnitBall E := by
  classical
  exact if h : ∀ i, T.Respects (I i) then
    f (ballMean hD (fun i =>
      partitionColor I hI hD f (T.restrict (I i) (h i))))
  else unitBallZero E
termination_by T.cellCount
decreasing_by
  exact T.restrict_cellCount_lt _ _ (hI _)
lean_source.note: No declaration docstring; the module docstring (RecursiveColoring.lean:6-11) reads: 'Recursive unit-ball colors of actual basic dyadic partitions. The recursion uses the number of actual cells. Restriction to any selected internal interval strictly decreases that number. The mean is bundled with its genuine unit-ball proof before it is supplied to the map.'

lean_source.name: partitionFamilyColor
lean_source.kind: def (coloring restricted to parent/child family, zero off admissibility)
lean_source.text:
/-- The family color is zero whenever the actual partition is inadmissible. -/
def partitionFamilyColor (hD : 0 < D) (f : UnitBall E → UnitBall E)
    (T : BasicPartition) (q : IntervalIndex D) : UnitBall E := by
  classical
  exact if h : PartitionAdmissible D T then
    partitionColor (selectedInterval D) (selectedInterval_internal D) hD f
      (T.restrict (familyInterval D q) (h q))
  else unitBallZero E

lean_source.name: partitionColor_restrict
lean_source.kind: theorem (defining recursive identity at a parent)
lean_source.text:
/-- Applying the recursion to a parent restriction gives the actual child mean.
The normalized two-step restriction is replaced by the proved composite one. -/
theorem partitionColor_restrict (I : Fin D → BasicInterval)
    (hI : ∀ i, (I i).Internal) (hD : 0 < D)
    (f : UnitBall E → UnitBall E) (T : BasicPartition) (i : Fin D)
    (hparent : T.Respects (I i))
    (hchild : ∀ j, T.Respects ((I i).comp (I j))) :
    partitionColor I hI hD f (T.restrict (I i) hparent) =
      f (ballMean hD (fun j => partitionColor I hI hD f
        (T.restrict ((I i).comp (I j)) (hchild j)))) := ...

lean_source.text:

    (h : PartitionAdmissible D T) (i : Fin D) :
    partitionFamilyColor hD f T (.inl i) =
      f (ballMean hD (fun j => partitionFamilyColor hD f T (.inr (i, j)))) := ...

speedup_targets.title: Monod's H(A) nonamenable, by rerunning the device on Farey (projective) cells
speedup_targets.statement: For a subring A of R, the group H(A) of piecewise-PSL_2(A) homeomorphisms of the projective line (breakpoints in the fixed-point set P_A) is nonamenable. The new case is A = Z; A != Z is Monod 2013.
speedup_targets.reference: Monod, PNAS 110 (2013) 4524-4527; Monod arXiv:2305.00796; Thurston (H_Q(Z) is isomorphic to F).
speedup_targets.status: A != Z: known (Monod, via Carriere-Ghys). A = Z: follows from 248 via Thurston's isomorphism.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: 4 pp. plus Carriere-Ghys (deep). The 2023 elementary route is about 8 pp. Not formalised.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: SKEPTICAL FINDING. The rerun works only on PSL_2(Z)-Farey cells. For A != Z the stabiliser in PSL_2(A) of a cell contains hyperbolic dilations x -> lambda^2 x (lambda a unit of A, e.g. 2 for Z[1/2]). So the projective renormalisation T_I is not unique, condition (a) (T_I)_J = T_{I.J} fails, and covariance under general g in H(A) is lost. The rerun therefore reproves nonamenability of Thurston's copy of F (projective model) and then needs the overgroup lemma. It is still a useful portability test, because the renormalisation changes from affine to projective. It does not remove the embedding of F; it only replaces the Minkowski-?-conjugation by a native projective run.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: low-med (removes Carriere-Ghys for every A, but only through the F copy)
speedup_targets.confidence: medium (that it works on PSL_2(Z) cells); high (that it cannot run natively on PSL_2(A) cells for A != Z)

It builds random finite polygonal partitions whose law is almost invariant, which works because its exchanges are translations (no scale change). The device explains why the same strategy must fail for F: scale-changing transports plus a recursive colouring rule out almost-invariant partition laws. A natural joint 'dichotomy' statement for the two families, and a proves-too-much control: the device cannot apply to F_m.

328 (Kirk's problem: every nonexpansive self-map of a bounded closed convex subset of a reflexive space has a fixed point): complementary. B-S maps are Lipschitz but not nonexpansive, so they are consistent with 328. The device needs L > 1, and the paper's D > 4L^2/delta^2 shows the cost of L. No reuse.
release_reuse.lean_notes_2026_10_09: The OAI library holds three separate amenability definitions: Thompson/Model.lean InvariantMean (248), SimpleAmenable/Model.lean FolnerAmenable (253, proved for polygonAlternatingGroup in about 85k lines), and Unitarizability/Model.lean Amenable (251). Cross-family Lean tests need equivalence lemmas, roughly 100-200 lines (MeanToFolner.lean already proves one direction for InvariantMean). No other OAI directory uses partitionColor or UnitBall-valued recursions.

top5.target: S1: F_n nonamenable by a direct n-adic rerun
top5.argument: This is the cleanest Lean speedup test available. The statement needs about 60-80 lines (copy Model.lean with base n), and there is an exact formal baseline: the 248 development (9457 lines, 572-declaration comparator DAG). The n-adic transports lie in F_n, not in an embedded copy of F, so the rerun is a genuine reuse of the definition rather than the overgroup lemma. The measurement is the prover budget with versus without partitionColor plus the generic core in L, with the embedding route (BCS plus overgroup lemma) as the control arm. Caveat: the qualitative result is already known via embedding, so this measures portability and cost, not new mathematics.

top5.target: S2: Stein F_{2,3} and F_tau by direct reruns
top5.argument: This is the same test as S1, but with mixed-arity or irrational cell geometry. It checks whether self-similar restriction and unique affine renormalisation, the two facts the definition rests on, survive a non-uniform branching factor. The statement takes under 300 lines and the baseline is again 248's Lean. It is lower priority than S1 because it adds plumbing cost without a new conceptual test.

This is the shortlist's named test. My analysis says it can only run on PSL_2(Z)-Farey cells. For A != Z, PSL_2(A) contains dilations fixing every cell, so the projective renormalisation is not unique and (T_I)_J = T_{I.J} fails. The rerun therefore reproves Thurston's projective copy of F and still needs the overgroup lemma; it cannot avoid embedding F. It remains worth running as an affine-to-projective portability test, and it would remove Carriere-Ghys from Monod's theorem. The statement takes under 300 lines (piecewise-Mobius carrier). There is no formal baseline.

top5.target: S4: explicit Folner constant for {x0, x1}
top5.argument: This has the highest mathematical payoff: the first explicit isoperimetric constant for F. It comes directly from the definition's explicit boundaryConstant formula, which Lean already proves by rfl. The statement takes under 300 lines (x0, x1 as DyadicPLWitness elements). The proof is the problem. The Lean's L and transports are Classical.choose, so it needs an effective separation constant, plus normal forms and word-length bounds for the transports. That is a major new library, so this is a discovery target rather than a cheap speedup test.

top5.target: S5: explicit Kesten bound for F
top5.argument: This is the shortlist's 'explicit Kesten-norm bound'. It is statable with under 300 lines (l^2 regular representation plus Mathlib's operator norm), but it needs S4 plus a discrete Cheeger/Kesten inequality for infinite graphs, which is absent from Mathlib. It ranks below S4 because it is strictly harder and adds no new use of the device.

precedent_check.verdict: No earlier equivalent found, so the N3 grade is not downgraded. The combination (recursive tree/partition colouring) + (vector values in an infinite-dimensional ball) + (Lipschitz map with no approximate fixed point) + (pair-exchangeability concentration) does not appear in the literature I could reach.
nearest_neighbours: Moore 2013, Ramsey characterisation: finite SCALAR colourings of finite binary trees with a convex Ramsey property. Neither recursive nor vector-valued; it is a reformulation, not a contradiction mechanism.

Moore, 'Fast growth in the Folner function for Thompson's group F' (arXiv:0905.1118): recursion over restrictions giving tower lower bounds on Folner sets. Scalar and unbounded, so it yields size bounds and no contradiction. This is the closest in spirit: the device is the bounded, non-stabilising upgrade of this recursion.
Akhmedov, height-function criteria (arXiv:0902.4755, 1310.4395): unbounded integer-valued heights. The device replaces 'height' by a bounded Lipschitz Hilbert-valued counter.
Monod 2013/2023: explicit fixed-point-free AFFINE convex compact spaces for H(A); by Monod's own statement the criterion fails precisely for F.
Day 1961, Gheysens-Monod 2017, Barroso-Mbombo-Pestov (arXiv:1410.8370): affine fixed-point characterisations. No nonlinear map, no recursion.
Benyamini-Sternfeld 1983 and Lin-Sternfeld 1985: the map itself, with no group-theoretic use.

Jones / Brothier-Jones Pythagorean representations: recursive assignment of Hilbert vectors along trees through a fixed LINEAR isometry. These are representations, not contradictions, and they have no averaging or fixed-point-free map. A structural cousin only.
Diaconis-Freedman finite de Finetti: the concentration step (EC2), not the definition.
